articles.title: Make in Bengaluru: Bullet train design ready, may hit tracks by May 2027
articles.summary: India’s indigenous bullet train B-28 design is complete; after squeeze tests and trials in Bengaluru and Surat, it may hit tracks by May 2027, says Vaishnaw.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Amid the country’s ambitious high-speed rail push, railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw Sunday said India’s indigenous bullet train B-28’s design has been completed. Following an inspection at the Aditya plant in Bharat Earth Movers Limited’s Tippasandra facility, he said the first train will be rolled out in 2027.The progress has been positive, Vaishnaw told TOI, adding that the indigenous design has already completed a squeeze test. “When the train moves at very high speed, a layer of vacuum is created around it. The entire atmospheric pressure comes onto the coach. That’s why the squeeze test is important, and it has now been completed,” he said.After the squeeze test, B-28 will be integrated with interior furniture. Vaishnaw said the train will be exposed to various climatic conditions.He said a dedicated track has been created in BEML’s Bengaluru facility to test the bullet train. “It will be first tested on that track, then it will be taken to Surat depot where there are slightly longer tracks for other tests,” he added.Vaishnaw said that the construction of the first section of the Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed rail corridor between Surat and Bilimora, targeted for launch by Aug 15, 2027, will be completed within the next two months.“This train will go onto the track somewhere around April or May next year. The construction is going on at a very good pace, both towards Ahmedabad and Mumbai. articles.title: Complaints galore, Maharashtra govt to let colleges delink from sole public technical education university
articles.summary: Maharashtra to amend DBATU Act, letting affiliated technical colleges de-link and join nearby universities after complaints over exams, delays and staffing issues.
articles.body: Mumbai: Maharashtra govt is set to amend the Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar Technological University (DBATU) Act, allowing affiliated colleges to leave the university and seek affiliation with another institution based on geographical location or return to their parent university.The proposed change marks a shift from the original vision for DBATU in Lonere, Raigad, as Maharashtra’s sole public university dedicated to technical education.Set up in 1989, DBATU was made the umbrella university for all affiliating technical colleges in 2014 through an amendment to the Act. And since 2017-18, affiliation with DBATU has been mandatory for all newly established technical colleges in the state offering engineering, pharmacy, management and architecture courses. It was optional for colleges established before 2017-18.Following repeated complaints from stakeholders over the conduct of examinations, delayed results and inadequate manpower, the state is planning to amend the DBATU Act to remove the mandatory affiliation clause for new colleges, allowing them to affiliate with universities based on their geographical location. The existing ones will also be given a choice if they wish to leave.The amendment allowing colleges to de-affiliate is a first for any public university in the state.The amendment bill, expected to be tabled during the upcoming winter session, will allow new engineering, pharmacy and MBA colleges from Mumbai, for instance, to seek affiliation with Mumbai University.The matter was brought up for discussion in the assembly on multiple occasions in the past. “Since 2017, we have been giving approval to new technical colleges only under DBATU. But there have been complaints for the last two years and political representatives have been seeking provision to de-affiliate, and therefore, we are planning to give them an option and bring in the amendment bill in the winter session,” said higher and technical education minister Chandrakant Patil during a media interaction. However, with the reforms taken up in the examination section and changes in the administration, the govt is confident about retaining most colleges.DBATU currently has 437 affiliated colleges across the state, including 22 in Mumbai. The highest numbers of affiliated colleges are in Nashik and Pune. A majority of the colleges affiliated to DBATU are pharmacy colleges, which mushroomed post-Covid.A principal of a college affiliated to DBATU cited the conduct of examinations, persistent delay in the announcement of results and marksheet issuance as major problems for the students from the technological university.This year, too, the situation was similar. The vice-chancellor, Prof Karbhari Kale, stepped down in March amid concern over delayed results. The govt then appointed Prof Rajanish Kamat as the acting VC. It also took up the task of announcing results on a war footing.Officials claimed that over 90% of the results of exams conducted in the summer session have already been announced. articles.title: Mumbai police impound BMW, seek digital media COO’s licence cancellation for ‘bid to run over’ traffic cop
articles.summary: Mumbai police impounded Juhi Mehta’s car after a Juhu crash; seek RTO licence cancellation for allegedly threatening and driving at a traffic cop in Vile Parle.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Juhu police have impounded the high-end car and asked the regional transport office to cancel the driving licence of Juhu resident Juhi Mehta, who had allegedly hit vehicles and threatened a traffic constable in Vile Parle (West) last week.Mehta, chief operating officer of an online media company, was booked for threatening and obstructing traffic constable Prashant Hake (36) and driving towards him after an accident at Sangeet Mahabharati Junction on Oct 30. She was arrested the next day and later granted bail.Police said fault in the accident remained unclear. Mehta claimed she was trying to park the car to the side to prevent congestion and was uncomfortable stepping out because several people were recording the incident.Hake, attached to Santacruz Traffic Division, said he was regulating traffic near Pratiksha Bungalow in Vile Parle West on Oct 30. Between 8.15pm and 8.30pm, he noticed a crowd gathering at Sangeet Mahabharati Junction. He went to the location and found that a high-end car (driven by Mehta) and a hatchback had had a collision and were blocking traffic.He directed both drivers to move their vehicles aside to clear the obstruction. Hake alleged that Mehta argued with him, verbally abused and threatened him, and tried to leave. When he stood in front of her high-end car and repeatedly asked her to stop, she allegedly accelerated towards him. Hake moved aside and escaped without injury.Mehta allegedly drove away at high speed towards JVPD Junction. A person at the scene recorded the incident, according to the complaint. The hatchback driver, Navinkumar Udaychand Jha (42), told Hake that the high-end car had hit his vehicle from behind. Hake observed damage to its boot, bumper, right taillight, sensor lock and paintwork.Joint commissioner of police, traffic division, Satyanarayan Chaudhary said necessary action was being taken under standard operating procedures.Deputy commissioner of police (Zone West-2) Mohit Garg said further procedures were under way.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: 7,000 offences in eight months: Pune records sharpest jump in drunk driving cases, police promise more patrols
articles.summary: Pune reports 7,379 drunk driving offences in Jan–Aug, up 12% over 2024 total; police to boost night patrols, random checks amid public safety concerns.
articles.body: Pune: A policewoman suspended earlier this week for allegedly driving under the influence. A viral video that shows a drunk motorist ramming into multiple two-wheelers. Pune’s problem of drunk driving is once again back in focus, with data now showing that as many as 7,379 offences were registered within just the first eight months of this year, 12% more than last year’s entire total (6,602 cases).The increase is even more alarming if one were to compare the data with 2023 figures, when only 562 cases were registered.Police officials TOI spoke to said the Jan-Aug numbers are indeed worrisome. “This year’s figures exceed those of all previous years,” said additional commissioner of police, Manoj Patil. “We have been working to control drunk driving, but our efforts have to be intensified, with greater emphasis on night patrols and random checks. This is a serious offence. Lives are at risk,” he said.Residents said drunk motorists were now a common sight in the city. “Almost every evening, we see obvious signs of a vehicle being driven by someone under the influence,” said Vishal Khatir, a working professional who lives in VimannagarHe said that last month he was almost assaulted by a group travelling in a car after he confronted them. “Bystanders came to my rescue. This group stopped the car, surrounded me and threatened to beat me up. Even their speech was slurring. And I have hardly ever seen police patrols in the area,” he said.Animesh Sherkha, a Koregaon Park resident, said drunk driving was commonplace in the area, despite police presence. “It’s indeed a problem, given the number of bars and restaurants here. It’s unfortunate that even after the Porsche incident (in 2024), city police have been unable to clamp down.”A retired RTO official TOI spoke to said a critical countermeasure could be cancellation of driving licences. “Just last month, the police actually recommended suspension or cancellation of around 1,700 driving licences for serious traffic violations, including drunk driving. In my view, the state government should consider allowing authorities to permanently cancel the licences of anyone caught driving under the influence, without the possibility of reissuance,” the retired official said, adding that such measures could be backed by tougher penalties, including vehicle confiscation, higher fines and imprisonment.Harshad Abhyankar, a member of the Save Pune Traffic Movement said it was time enforcement moved beyond routine checks and fines. “Drink driving is often treated as an issue of indiscipline, prompting the usual suggestions of increased surveillance and higher fines. A dedicated campaign over several months can help curb the problem, but authorities also need to think differently and explore innovative measures,” he said.Salunke Vihar Road resident Atul Pirodkar highlighted another concern: open drinking near liquor shops. “A good example is the shop near my house. I see people drinking in the open every day. Surely, the police are aware of the problem. articles.title: Over Rs 960cr scam? 127 plots sold, then mortgaged to scam-hit bank in Bengaluru
articles.summary: Fresh fraud allegations hit Bengaluru’s scam-hit Sri Guru Raghavendra Sahakara Bank as 127 already-sold Shankara Layout plots were mortgaged; dues pegged at Rs 961 crore.
articles.body: BENGALURU: More than five years after Sri Guru Raghavendra Sahakara Bank Niyamitha in south Bengaluru went bust leaving hundreds of depositors in dire straits, fresh allegations of fraud have come to light, with properties already sold to unsuspecting buyers having been mortgaged with the bank.In one case, the outstanding amount against the mortgaged property is Rs 961 crore even though the value of the collateral is not known.According to officials, the bank does not have accurate information about the value of these properties, which are spread across the city and cover 45 to 50 acres. The farthest property mortgaged to the bank is in Chintamani, Kolar.Documents in possession of TOI show a Bangalore Development Authority-approved Sri Shankara Layout in Kambipura village, Kengeri hobli of Bengaluru, was mortgaged along with 127 plots that had already been sold to innocent individuals.The layout has a registered residents’ welfare association, whose members say they learnt of the mortgage only recently.On July 16, 2026, the layout owners’ welfare association wrote a letter to the administrator of Sri Guru Raghavendra Sahakara Bank Niyamitha and said that between 2011 and 2015, there was an absolute sale deed executed by the developers of the layout with each of the 127 individuals.The letter acknowledged as received by the bank administrator said two mortgage deeds registered and dated Oct 31, 2019, and two rectification deeds of Nov 28, 2019… along with residential plots formed on them in entirety, were shown as collateral security to your bank which was then represented by then chief advisor M Vasudev Maiya to obtain huge amounts of loans from the bank.The association asked how the bank could have accepted the plots as collateral when absolute sale deeds had already been executed in the buyers’ favour.It claimed the case involved criminal breach of trust by the developers, allegedly in connivance with bank officials at the time. The association urged the bank administrator not to initiate any proceedings or take steps which may damage or dent their interest, rights and stake over the physical possession of their respective residential plots.A notice issued by the bank to the layout’s developers in Jan 2026 said loans totalling Rs 739 crore and 87 lakh had been raised by mortgaging the property to various persons. With interest, the outstanding amount was Rs 961 crore.Bank officials, on condition of anonymity, told TOI that in as many as 10 to 15 cases of property mortgages, the then bank officials had attached “unsecured” loans to evade audit lacunae.“These accounts are being termed ‘rollover accounts’, wherein unsecured loans were being attached to mortgaged properties. While the actual loan recipient would have received Rs 10 to Rs 12 crore, the rest of the loan amount was given out to other people,” said one senior bank official.In the case of Shankara Layout developers, 23 people apart from the original loan recipients were given money. Beneficiaries of these loans include individuals and companies.On Shankara Layout, bank officials said they would take a factual position on whether the Sri Shankara Layout plots were sold before or after the land was mortgaged in 2019. “Properties sold prior to the mortgaged dates cannot be included in the recovery process,” said officials, adding that the plot owners were sending their documents individually to the bank.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bengaluru | Silver Rate in Bengaluru | Bank Holidays in Bengaluru | Public Holidays in Bengaluru | Bengaluru AQI | Weather in Bengaluru | Petrol Price in Bengaluru | Diesel Price in Bengaluru | CNG Price in Bengaluru | LPG Price in BengaluruStay updated with the latest Bengaluru news. articles.title: PMLA case: Azam Khan sent to 14-day judicial custody, day after release from jail
articles.summary: Azam Khan remanded to 14-day judicial custody by Ghaziabad PMLA court, lodged in Dasna jail after ED arrest in 2019 money laundering case.
articles.body: LUCKNOW: Senior Samajwadi Party member and former MP Azam Khan was remanded to 14 days judicial custody by a special Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) court in Ghaziabad on Sunday. He will be lodged at Dasna district jail in Ghaziabad instead of Rampur jail, from where he had been released a day earlier.The Enforcement Directorate produced Azam Khan before Special Judge Anti-Corruption CBI court, Avanish Kumar Pandey, around 10.30am amid tight security. A convoy of five ED vehicles brought him to the court premises, accompanied by more than 100 personnel from the CRPF and the Uttar Pradesh Police.Khan appeared calm when he arrived at the court. As he rolled down the window, journalists asked whether he wanted to say something. He responded, “Ab kya reh gaya hai bolne ko” (What is left to say now?).The court gave the order after hearing the matter for about 90 minutes. ED counsel Kuldeep Srivastava argued on behalf of the agency while ED’s deputy director Piyush Thorat and assistant director Praveen Kumar remained present inside the court.ED had arrested the SP veteran on Saturday evening in connection with a money laundering case registered by the agency in 2019. He was taken into custody after being released from Rampur jail and was taken to the ED headquarters in Delhi for questioning.Thereafter, Azam complained of chest and stomach ache, following which a team of CRPF and ED took him to RML hospital in Delhi for a medical checkup. After clearance from a specialist team of doctors, he was brought to ED HQ and questioned again.According to officials, Azam was questioned at length in connection with the alleged misuse of govt funds in the construction of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur. During the interrogation, the agency reportedly put more than 50 questions to him.Azam and his son Abdullah Azam had walked out of Rampur jail around 7.15pm on Saturday after spending nearly 11 months in custody. His release came after the Allahabad high court on Oct 29 suspended his 10-year sentence in the two PAN card cases.However, his release proved short-lived as the ED arrested him in the money laundering case.The developments triggered sharp political reactions. Uttar Pradesh energy Minister AK Sharma said the law applies equally to everyone, irrespective of their position or identity. He said that people sometimes disregard the law when they become consumed by the arrogance of power, but eventually everyone has to face its consequences.Meanwhile, Samajwadi Party national general secretary Shivpal Yadav alleged that the ED acted at govt’s behest to arrest Azam Khan and asked people to speak out against oppressive govts.BJP members, on the other hand, defended the ED action, saying that the law was equal for everyone. articles.title: SC upholds HC order allowing I-T to reassess income of ex-CJI's sons
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Holding that the income tax department is not precluded from conducting reassessment upon discovering evidence suggesting income had escaped
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Holding that the income tax department is not precluded from conducting reassessment upon discovering evidence suggesting income had escaped assessment, Supreme Court upheld a Delhi high court order allowing the agency to reassess the income of the sons of former Chief Justice of India YK Sabharwal for 2008-09 and 2009-10.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran dismissed the Sabharwals' appeal and said the notice issued by the department in 2015 was valid as it was based on reasons duly recorded and on tangible material of a report of its investigation unit.2015 notice of assessing officer issued on reasons duly recorded and is valid: SCRecording details of financial transactions, the Supreme Court bench noted Chetan Sabharwal along with his brother Nitin Sabharwal and two other shareholders entered into two share purchase agreements with GYS Real Estate Pvt Ltd (buyer company) for a sale of 7.5 lakh equity shares of Pawan Impex (P) Ltd and 2.5 lakh equity shares of SVIIT Software (P) Ltd held by each of the parties for a sale consideration of Rs 195 crore and Rs 60 crore, respectively. The appellant and other selling shareholders were each entitled to 1/4th share of the total consideration. "We are of the firm view that the impugned notice dated March 31, 2015, issued by the assessing officer under Section 148 of Income Tax Act, for initiating reassessment for assessment years 2008-09 and 2009-10, was issued on reasons duly recorded and is valid," the bench said."The reasons rest on tangible material, namely the report of the DGIT Investigation Unit, Noida, which concluded that shares of company No. 1 (Pawan Impex (P) Ltd) and company No. 2 (SVIIT Software (P) Ltd) were overvalued when compared with the cost of their land and building, and they have a rational nexus and a live link with the belief formed by the assessing officer," it said.Subsequent to completion of assessment, the investigation unit conducted enquiries into the value of the shares of Pawan Impex (P) Ltd and SVIIT Software (P) Ltd and prepared a report. The report concluded, prima facie, that the shares were overvalued when compared with the cost of their land and building, which was much lower than the transaction amounts of Rs 195 crore and Rs 60 crore, respectively.The enquiries revealed the appellants purchased one-half share of the property at Sikandara Road, Delhi, in April 2010 through a court auction, and that the major source of this investment was the sale proceeds of the shares of the companies. On perusal of the investigation report and after a gap of four years, the department issued a notice under Section 148 of the act for reassessment.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Mayday mayday': Videos show moment Florida jet crashed near busy road
articles.summary: Videos recorded by motorists captured the moment a business jet carrying nine people plunged from the sky and exploded into a fireball near a busy roadway
articles.body: Videos recorded by motorists captured the moment a business jet carrying nine people plunged from the sky and exploded into a fireball near a busy roadway in Florida on Sunday. All nine people aboard the aircraft were killed, US transportation secretary Sean Duffy said as cited by news agency AP.The Bahamas-bound Learjet 60 crashed in Greenacres, in Palm Beach County, narrowly missing nearby homes and passing vehicles. The impact left a large crater on the roadside, with flames and thick black smoke engulfing the area.Air traffic control recordings reveal the desperate final moments of the flight, as the pilot reported worsening weather conditions, turbulence and ice accumulating on the aircraft before issuing distress calls."We have light, clear ice that is manageable and moderate turbulence," the pilot initially told air traffic controllers.The situation deteriorated rapidly after the aircraft encountered precipitation and requested permission to climb 2,000 feet. The jet began losing altitude at an alarming rate, prompting the pilot to declare an emergency."We're descending 8,000 – mayday, mayday - we're descending 10,000 feet per minute," the pilot radioed.The pilot later reported that the aircraft was in an overspeed condition as its descent accelerated."We are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000 feet per minute," the pilot said before adding, "We're going to crash into the ground."According to air traffic control recordings and flight-tracking data, the aircraft had been flying east at 35,000 feet when it encountered turbulence, icing and precipitation. It subsequently entered a steep dive, with its descent rate reaching 30,000 feet per minute.Duffy said the Learjet crashed at 12:50 pm and described the incident as a "horrific tragedy". The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is sending a team to assist the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) with the investigation.Florida Governor Ron DeSantis said there were no immediate reports of injuries or deaths among people on the ground."It was a cataclysmic plane crash," DeSantis told reporters at the scene. "It looked like a missile going down and left a big crater on the side of the road."Authorities were evacuating around 600 people from a nearby mobile home community as a precaution. The road was also closed until further notice.The aircraft had taken off from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to the Bahamas, the FAA said. The identities of those aboard and the exact cause of the crash were not immediately known.The crash occurred as heavy rain battered the region, with a flood watch in effect until Monday afternoon, according to the National Weather Service.You use AI every day. articles.title: Delhi’s Rs 99cr plan to box in Yamuna raises red flags
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Delhi govt’s plan to build a 4.7-km reinforced concrete wall along Yamuna has raised concerns among experts, who warn that the intervention
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi govt’s plan to build a 4.7-km reinforced concrete wall along Yamuna has raised concerns among experts, who warn that the intervention could restrict movement of floodwater, alter the river’s natural flow and potentially shift flood risks to other areas.Approved as part of a Rs 622-crore flood-control plan, the wall, estimated to cost Rs 99 crore, is likely to run from Magazine Road drain to Old Railway Bridge. The six-to-seven-foot-high structure is intended to protect vulnerable low-lying areas from inundation.But experts argue the project risks treating the symptoms rather than addressing why Yamuna has been reaching high levels even at comparatively lower upstream discharges.In Sept 2025, the river reached nearly 207.5 metres at Delhi’s railway bridge, while discharge at Hathnikund Barrage was reported at around 3.2 lakh cusecs. During the July 2023 floods, it rose to a record 208.66 m at a reported discharge of around 3.5 lakh cusecs.Experts say these patterns warrant investigation into changes in the river’s carrying capacity, floodplain encroachment, riverbed conditions and the cumulative impact of infrastructure.A senior govt official, who requested anonymity, questioned the logic of adding another barrier to an already constrained river. “When a river channel is already encroached upon, with buildings occupying its floodplain, putting up walls further restricts floodwater and can cause water levels to rise. Unequal pressure could even cause a wall to fail, potentially leading to catastrophic consequences,” the official said, warning that the risks needed careful assessment before construction.Pointing out that while such experiments work in Europe where rivers have consistent natural or environmental flow round the year, environmentalist Diwan Singh said the intervention in a largely monsoon-fed and restricted river like Yamuna could undermine the natural functioning.“This will hinder the natural flow of the river and aggravate flooding. It will make it more like a canal, which is not suitable for a monsoonal river such as Yamuna. Its floodplains exist to accommodate unpredictable flows. Tampering with their shape and size will be bad for both the river and Delhi,” he said.The concerns are significant given the existing network of bridges, barrages, embankments and riverside roads. A Central Water Commission 2025 study on Delhi’s 2023 floods recommends suitable flood protection at vulnerable locations, including Nili Chhatri, but does not specifically recommend the proposed 4.7-km concrete-reinforced wall. Its modelling also found that replacing certain existing lateral embankments with structures raised on piers could reduce water levels at some locations.Similar concerns have been raised over Delhi’s proposed 22-km Yamuna riverfront project, where experts stress the need to prioritise river restoration and floodplain protection over interventions that could further constrain the river.Govt’s wider flood-control plan includes spending Rs 260 crore on proposed biomining projects to process silt removed from major drains. While improved drainage may help reduce waterlogging, experts say it cannot replace a comprehensive assessment of the river’s carrying capacity and floodplain connectivity.“Construction of the wall should be reconsidered until the ongoing topographic and bathymetric surveys are completed. The changing relationship between upstream discharge and water levels in Delhi warrants an independent investigation into the river’s carrying capacity and the cumulative impact of existing infrastructure,” said Bhim Singh Rawat, associate coordinator of South Asia Network on Dams, Rivers and People (SANDRP).You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Months before taking control of hundreds of fridges at French supermarkets, did hackers break into the US army freezers; Pentagon classifies it as ...
articles.summary: The Pentagon is investigating whether a cyberattack triggered a series of commercial freezer failures that spoiled food across multiple US military bases
articles.body: The Pentagon is investigating whether a cyberattack triggered a series of commercial freezer failures that spoiled food across multiple US military bases in August, according to a US official familiar with the matter. The disruptions hit approximately six commissaries -- the on-base grocery stores serving service members and their families -- the official said, speaking on the condition of anonymity to discuss an ongoing probe. At Fort Huachuca in Arizona, base officials discovered that a walk-in freezer had unexpectedly shifted into defrost mode, heating its inventory and ruining the stored provisions.The US Cyber Command and Defense Department law enforcement agencies are leading the inquiry. Investigators have not publicly identified any suspects or formally confirmed the technical root cause behind the equipment failures. Reuters first reported Thursday that investigators were treating the incidents as a possible hack. It’s unclear who might be responsible or whether investigators have conclusively determined what caused the failures.The US investigators are also coordinating with French authorities. Earlier this month, hackers manipulated temperature controls on commercial cooling systems across more than 350 locations in France, forcing widespread inventory disposal at local supermarkets.What happened in FranceIn early October, hackers targeted hundreds of French supermarkets in a cyberattack that reportedly caused refrigerators and freezers to overheat, spoiling food and sparking fires.Fridges at French supermarket chains Carrefour, Monoprix, the Les Mousquetaires-owned Intermarche, and Cooperative U, among others, all saw fridges heat up to as much as 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit) overnight. The incident highlights growing vulnerabilities in operational technology—the internet-connected industrial control systems that regulate everyday supply chain infrastructure. While critical infrastructure discussions often center on power grids and water treatment facilities, cybersecurity analysts warn that food storage systems frequently rely on remote-access controls protected by weak defenses.Food and Agriculture Information Sharing and Analysis Center's warningThe Food and Agriculture Information Sharing and Analysis Center (ISAC), an industry threat-intelligence group, has repeatedly warned that internet-accessible industrial controls present an easy target for malicious actors. Because the food sector cannot tolerate extended downtime without severe financial and logistical losses, facilities remain prime targets for extortion and ransomware campaigns. A 2021 Department of Homeland Security assessment similarly warned that cyber-induced refrigeration failures posed direct risks to national food distribution networks.The August commissary failures were first noted publicly by the Signal and Silence blog, followed by reporting from Stars and Stripes on the military's involvement and The Telegraph on international coordination with France. In Congress, the incidents have renewed momentum around supply chain security. Lawmakers reintroduced the bipartisan Farm and Food Cybersecurity Act in 2025, aiming to bolster crisis response protocols and federal threat-sharing mechanisms across the nation’s agricultural and distribution pipelines.You use AI every day. articles.body: Ukraine and Russia have reported cyberattacks targeting their emergency alert systems, with hackers allegedly circulating fake warnings of radiation, chemical and nuclear threats, raising concerns over the disruption of public safety communications amid the ongoing war between the two countries.Ukraine's air raid alert application was reportedly compromised on Sunday, sending false warnings about chemical and radiation threats to mobile phones across the country. Loudspeaker systems in Kyiv also broadcast similar messages, prompting the Ukrainian Air Force to warn of possible external interference."Attention. The Air Alert app has likely been compromised," the Air Force said on Telegram, adding that, "There is no radiation threat! Stay calm and follow our updates on our channel!"Ukraine's Central Intelligence Agency also reported a failure in the application and urged residents to consult alternative sources of information to verify warnings about possible air strikes.However, the Ministry of Digital Transformation later said the nationwide alert system was functioning normally."The nationwide alert system is operating in normal mode. All threat signals are transmitted to regional administrations and, accordingly, to street alert systems," the ministry said in a post on X.Meanwhile, Russia's Ministry of Emergency Situations said its mobile application had been targeted in a massive cyberattack that enabled attackers to distribute false public safety information. Russian authorities also reported fake warnings about nuclear strikes inside the country, with a Ukrainian espionage group reportedly suspected of involvement."The Russian Ministry of Emergency Situations' mobile app was subjected to a massive cyberattack, which allowed the attackers to distribute fake information to the public," the ministry said in a statement.According to TASS, the ministry said efforts were underway to eliminate the vulnerability in the application and restore its normal functioning.The incidents come amid continuing military operations and diplomatic efforts surrounding the Russia-Ukraine conflict. The false alerts in Ukraine were reportedly circulated shortly before the end of a localised ceasefire in the Oleshky area of Ukraine's Kherson region.On Sunday, US First Lady Melania Trump commended Moscow and Kyiv for their cooperation during the five-day humanitarian ceasefire, which concluded on November 1. articles.title: Caste, religion, complexion, height and education: How Hyderabad fertility racket handpicked egg donors; women recruited from 7 states, offered up to Rs 50,000
articles.summary: HYDERABAD: Women recruited from seven states for alleged commercial egg donation were being matched with prospective recipients based on specific
articles.body: HYDERABAD: Women recruited from seven states for alleged commercial egg donation were being matched with prospective recipients based on specific requirements such as caste, religion, complexion, height, education and geographical background, said Malkajgiri police officials who busted a fertility racket in the city on Saturday.The accused allegedly operated a network of agents across the country who exchanged information about prospective donors through WhatsApp groups and other communication channels. Whenever couples seeking egg donors approached them with specific requirements, the agents circulated the details within their network to identify suitable women."The accused exploit women who are in need of money. They have WhatsApp groups and other means for exchanging information with a network of people across India. Whenever they receive enquiries from people looking for egg donors, the requirements are shared with illegal agents in the network,'' Begumpet inspector P Saidulu told TOI.Investigators said the prime accused, Amit Sharma, and his associates recruited women from seven different states: West Bengal, Chhattisgarh, Delhi, Assam, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand and Odisha. The accused allegedly operated under the cover of running women's hostels. Police suspect that the accommodation facilities were, in reality, being used to house prospective egg donors before they were taken to IVF centres for procedures..Investigators said the demands of prospective recipients determined the compensation offered to donors. While some women were allegedly promised Rs 20,000 to Rs 30,000, certain donors were offered as much as ₹50,000, depending on the requirements of the couples seeking eggs."The couples seeking donors specify their preferences, including complexion, caste, height and other characteristics. Based on our interactions with the accused and rescued women, complexion and regional background appear to be among the more common requirements. The agents circulate these demands within their network to identify women who match the criteria. The more specific the requirements, the higher the amount charged," an investigating officer said.Police said referrals from previous donors were a key source of recruitment. The investigation has also turned towards the role of IVF centres allegedly linked to the network. articles.title: Learning over drinks: How Bengaluru’s bars and pubs are becoming spaces for intellectual debate
articles.summary: Political and philosophical debates during the french revolution often unfolded in taverns, cafés and pubs.
articles.body: Political and philosophical debates during the french revolution often unfolded in taverns, cafés and pubs. Alcohol consumption was central to social life, and these establishments became spaces where ideas were exchanged and debated. In bengaluru, where alcohol remains a familiar social lubricant, some bars and pubs are now serving a purpose beyond the weekend pub crawl.In a country where education is often associated with academic requirements, grades and cut-offs, a growing number of people are exploring learning for its own sake. Events such as ‘lectures over drinks’ offer an anti-utilitarian approach to education — the kind of learning pursued simply for the joy of discovering something new.Third spaces for a busy city“For a city like bengaluru, i think bars and parks are the only third spaces,” say the co-founders of pint of view, shruti sah and harsh sne hanshu, who also founded cubbon reads. “The city works almost around the clock, and a huge part of people’s remaining time is spent commuting between work and home. With the pressure of work and infrastructure that doesn’t always give you enough time or space for yourself, communities like pint of view can give you some time off from active participation.”Bengaluru is home to some of the country’s leading institutions in science, the arts and public policy. But the founders of pint of view believe there is a disconnect between these institutions and the wider public. “These institutions produce incredible work, but they can often feel quite gatekept. It can be difficult to simply walk into a lecture at an institution when you need an id card or have to be affiliated with it,” they say. Inspired by the us-based lectures on tap series — and tired of waiting for it to come to india — they decided to create their own version.Learning beyond the ordinaryThese are not the conventional classrooms where students once had to ask permission even to drink water during a lecture. Bars are strategic venues for such events: they are centrally located, close to where much of the working population spends time and convenient for those looking to unwind after work with a beer or a cosmopolitan while learning about artificial intelligence, geopolitics, the human brain or almost any subject imaginable.Ronit, an independent filmmaker who has attended lectures over drinks, says the events have helped him meet new people and build connections. “You can watch videos online about different topics that might interest or challenge you. But the offline experience is a whole lot better. You get to ask questions, the speakers respond, and that creates a kind of bond for the duration that you’re in the room,” he says.Another attendee, aditi, draws a distinction between these events and typical classroom lectures. “The speakers are also there because they want to be, not because a job compels them to. They know there’ll be questions from people with diverse backgrounds, so they’re ready for it,” she says.“At brydge, we wanted to go beyond the ordinary events that happen,” say siya pravin sarnaik and atharva atul rampure, the co-founders of brydge, which started intellect on ice.The duo were studying in the uk when they noticed people gathering around niche interests — from specific cuisines to books — something they felt was missing back home. Intellect on ice began in mumbai and has since expanded to bengaluru, delhi and pune. “We felt offline experiences had the potential to be more enriching and that people needed to come together in a more meaningful way. We wanted to create a space to get your thoughts going,” says siya. The events do not follow a fixed format. The team decides which topics to explore, conducts research and then reaches out to people with the expertise and ideas to share. “It’s not a very structured event, but that is the whole point. The experiential economy is booming, and it is in need of infrastructure,” she says.A room where ideas can breatheThe contrarian debate club, co-founded by school friends sudarshan senthil kumar and srinthan hampi, has also taken intellectual pursuits to bengaluru’s bars and pubs, including woodside inn and big pitcher.The founders wanted to recreate the old british aesthetic of institutions such as the oxford union society. Sudarshan wanted to continue participating in debates after college, while srinthan had been involved in debates and model united nations conferences throughout his life. Together, they wanted to create a space where people could express their thoughts freely and engage in meaningful discussion.“One of the few rooms in bengaluru where no one is going to scream at you,” says sudarshan. He believes good ideas often emerge only after several bad ones have been aired. “To arrive at a good idea, you must go through six or seven bad ones,” he says.Participants are welcome to bring their ideas to the table, as long as they are willing to keep an open mind and listen to others.The club was initially meant to be a gathering of seven or eight friends. But the venue needed a larger crowd for the event to be viable. When the founders invited people on social media at short notice, the idea took off, attracting more than 100 entries.Finding the right scaleFor intellect on ice, one of the initial challenges was finding bars willing to allocate their entire space to a single organiser. Word of mouth, however, proved powerful. The first event, featuring a philosophy professor in a small mumbai bar, took off immediately.“Lectures on tap was also very visible on social media around the same time, so it was the right place at the right time,” says siya. The organisers are taking different approaches to scale.Pint of view plans to expand its lectures to audiences of between 100 and 300 people. It is also organising what it describes as asia’s first lecture festival, a two-day event at jayamahal palace grounds on dec 19 and 20, featuring a series of lectures and an expected audience of up to 5,000.Intellect on ice, on the other hand, plans to remain a more intimate gathering, with between 40 and 60 participants.There is also a shift in the way bars and pubs position themselves, now branching out into more than just drinks. Shane mannas, general manager, big pitcher indiranagar, says that for them, it is about marketing, and people getting to know about the brand. “After such events, we also get repeat guests, who later come with their families and friends as well,” says shane. “To make profits, especially on a usually busy time for us like weekends, we put a cover charge per head, giving the attendees a coupon they can redeem on food and drinks.” They hold a lot of other events as well, like kitty parties and corporate events.The ticket prices for these experiences range from early bird tickets starting at rs 599 that go live first, going up to rs 1,299. The attendees are mostly people from 25 to 40 years of age, including academics, working professionals, vcs, founders, doctors, lawyers, engineers and cas.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bengaluru | Silver Rate in Bengaluru | Bank Holidays in Bengaluru | Public Holidays in Bengaluru | Bengaluru AQI | Weather in Bengaluru | Petrol Price in Bengaluru | Diesel Price in Bengaluru | CNG Price in Bengaluru | LPG Price in BengaluruStay updated with the latest Bengaluru news. articles.summary: LUDHIANA: Two days after returning from Australia, a man allegedly stabbed his wife to death at their house in Vikas Nagar on Pakhowal Road.
articles.body: LUDHIANA: Two days after returning from Australia, a man allegedly stabbed his wife to death at their house in Vikas Nagar on Pakhowal Road. Police said the man suspected his wife of infidelity and stabbed her multiple times in the stomach and neck with a kitchen knife. Before committing the murder, the man sent their son to the market to get milk.The victim was identified as Kamaldeep Kaur, 49, and the accused as her husband, Ravinder Singh, 50, who works as a pick-up van driver. Dugri police have apprehended the accused.The incident occurred late Saturday when the couple was at home with their elder son, Gagandeep Singh. Their younger son lives in Australia, and the couple had gone there to meet him. While Kamaldeep had returned about four months ago, Ravinder returned to India two days ago.Gagandeep said that his parents had been behaving normally for the past two days and had not fought. Late Saturday, his father asked him to get milk from the market. He left the house and, on returning, saw his father running out of the house. When he asked what had happened, his father told him to go inside and check.Gagandeep rushed inside and saw his mother lying on the bed in a pool of blood. He raised an alarm and sought help from neighbours to rush his mother to the hospital. The woman was taken to the hospital, where doctors declared her dead.Inspector Gurmukh Singh, SHO of Dugri police station, said, "The accused used a kitchen knife to stab his wife to death. He attacked her in the stomach and neck multiple times. The police suspect that the man had returned to India with a plan to kill his wife as he executed the murder two days after his return."The inspector added that a murder case had been registered against the accused, who had been taken into custody. Initial investigations suggest that suspicion of infidelity was the motive behind the murder. articles.summary: A private Learjet 60 carrying nine people plunged into a South Florida neighbourhood and exploded into a massive fireball, leaving a huge crater near a
articles.body: A private Learjet 60 carrying nine people plunged into a South Florida neighbourhood and exploded into a massive fireball, leaving a huge crater near a busy roadway in Greenacres, Florida. All nine people aboard the aircraft were killed in the crash, while authorities reported no immediate casualties on the ground.Dramatic videos recorded by motorists captured the aircraft nosediving towards the ground before erupting into flames near homes and passing vehicles. Thick black smoke engulfed the crash site, while burning debris and chunks of pavement were scattered around the crater.Describing the impact, Florida Governor Ron DeSantis said the aircraft appeared to come down like a missile."It was a cataclysmic plane crash," DeSantis told reporters at the scene. "It looked like a missile going down and left a big crater on the side of the road."US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy confirmed that all nine people aboard had died. In a post on X, he said the Learjet 60 crashed in Palm Beach County at 12:50 pm and described the incident as a "horrific tragedy".The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is sending a team to assist the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) in investigating the crash. Authorities have not yet established what caused the aircraft to go down.What happened in the jet's final moments?Air traffic control recordings have provided a glimpse into the aircraft's final moments, with the pilot reporting icing, turbulence and precipitation before the jet entered a steep descent.According to flight tracking data and air traffic control communications captured by LiveATC.net, the aircraft was flying east at 35,000 feet when the pilot reported turbulence and ice accumulation. The crew requested permission to climb another 2,000 feet."We have light, clear ice that is manageable and moderate turbulence," the pilot told air traffic controllers.However, the situation deteriorated rapidly. The aircraft began losing altitude at an accelerating rate, with its descent reaching 10,000 feet per minute before increasing to 20,000 feet and eventually 30,000 feet per minute, according to flight tracking data and air traffic control recordings.The pilot declared an emergency and issued distress calls as the aircraft continued its rapid descent."We’re descending 8,000 – mayday, mayday - we’re descending 10,000 feet per minute," the pilot radioed.Moments later, the pilot reported that the aircraft had entered an overspeed condition, indicating that it was exceeding its operating speed limits."We are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000 feet per minute," the pilot radioed, before adding, "We’re going to crash into the ground."The aircraft then banked sharply to the right before plunging into the ground near the roadway.What we know about the Florida plane crashAccording to the FAA, the Learjet 60 had departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to the Bahamas. Jim Reynolds, a spokesperson for the Austin airport, confirmed that the aircraft was privately operated but could not immediately provide details about those aboard.The crash occurred in Greenacres, a city of around 45,000 people located about seven miles southwest of West Palm Beach.Palm Beach County authorities began evacuating around 600 people from a nearby mobile home community as emergency teams responded to the incident and federal officials prepared to investigate.Authorities also closed the affected roadway until further notice. DeSantis said there were no immediate reports of injuries or deaths among people on the ground.The crash occurred amid heavy rainfall across the region, with the National Weather Service having issued a flood watch due to excessive rainfall through Monday afternoon.You use AI every day. articles.title: Ved Rahi, director of ‘Gul Gulshan Gulfam’, passes away
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Noted writer-filmmaker Ved Rahi, who directed pictures like ‘Prem Parbat’ and ‘Kali Ghata’, and the popular TV serial ‘Gul Gulshan Gulfam’, passed
articles.body: MUMBAI: Noted writer-filmmaker Ved Rahi, who directed pictures like ‘Prem Parbat’ and ‘Kali Ghata’, and the popular TV serial ‘Gul Gulshan Gulfam’, passed away at the age of 93 on Sunday.His skills as author and poet drew from a rare command over Hindi and his native Dogri.Ved Rahi was born in May 1933 in Jammu to Mulk Raj Saraf, a pioneering journalist of the state. He attained prominence as a Dogri writer in his hometown, following which he decided to move to Mumbai to test the might of his penmanship.Rahi’s success spanned over 25 films. His fame arose from having written the screenplay or dialogues of movies like ‘Yeh Raat Phir Na Aayegi’, ‘Pavitra Paapi’, ‘Aap Aaye Bahaar Aayi’, ‘Beimaan’, ‘Mome Ki Gudiya’, ‘Sanyasi’, ‘Charas’ and the sparkling ‘Bezubaan’.As his career blossomed, Rahi took the leap into direction with films like ‘Prem Parbat’ (Yeh dil aur unki nigaahon ke saaye), ‘Kali Ghata’ (Shashi Kapoor, Rekha) and recently, ‘Veer Savarkar’ in 2001. Sadly, both ‘Prem Parbat’ and ‘Kali Ghata’ are lost to viewers.Rahi was a familiar name on Doordarshan through the 1980s and 1990s thanks to serials like ‘Gul Gulshan Gulfam’, ‘Meera’, ‘Katha Sagar’, ‘Zindagi’, ‘Ehsaas’ and ‘Rishtey’.His former neighbour at New Sarvottam Society in Irla said, “He stayed here in Andheri for very long. But since many years he was with one of his two daughters. I remember that the print of his movie ‘Kali Ghata’ got destroyed in a fire. He had assisted Ramanand Sagar after he came to Mumbai. Several people from his production house bought flats in Sarvottam society.”Rahi won the Sahitya Akademi Award for his Dogri short story collection ‘Aale’ followed by the Rahul Sankrityayan Award and the Kusumagraj Rashtriya Sahitya Puraskar.He is survived by two daughters Anju Patel and Poonam Advani.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.summary: Missile defence systems have been deployed near US President Donald Trump's Mar-a-Lago residence and at Palm Beach International Airport in Florida, with
articles.body: Missile defence systems have been deployed near US President Donald Trump's Mar-a-Lago residence and at Palm Beach International Airport in Florida, with viral visuals showing military equipment positioned on a barge close to the presidential estate.The deployment comes ahead of Tuesday's US midterm elections, amid what the US Secret Service has described as a "heightened threat environment".Photographs taken last week showed two Avenger Air Defence Systems positioned on a barge in the waters near Mar-a-Lago, Trump's primary residence and resort in Palm Beach. US service members in military fatigues were also seen in the vicinity, The Independent reported.An Avenger system was also installed on the southern side of Palm Beach International Airport, recently renamed Donald J. Trump International Airport, according the South Florida Sun Sentinel.The North American Aerospace Defense Command (NORAD) confirmed to WPBF that the defence systems had been installed "in and around" Mar-a-Lago.Secret Service cites heightened threat environmentA Secret Service spokesperson said the agency had adjusted its protective arrangements in response to the security environment."The US Secret Service is operating in a heightened threat environment, and we continuously adapt our protective operations to incorporate cutting-edge tools, technology, and methods to safeguard our protectees," the spokesperson told The Independent.The spokesperson added, "At the request of the US Secret Service, NORAD and US Northern Command are providing Counter-Unmanned Aircraft System capabilities in support of our protective operations."The Avenger is a mobile air defence system designed to counter aerial threats. The platform is mounted on a Humvee and uses short-range Stinger missiles and a .50-calibre machine gun to engage low-altitude aerial threats, including aircraft and unmanned aerial vehicles.Aircraft intercepted near Mar-a-LagoThe deployment comes amid heightened tensions with Iran in the Middle East and follows a series of airspace security incidents near the Florida estate.Last week, while Trump was in Florida, a fighter jet intercepted a civilian aircraft that had entered restricted airspace over Mar-a-Lago.NORAD said the fighter jet carried out a standard "headbutt" manoeuvre to draw the pilot's attention, after which the civilian aircraft established communication and safely left the restricted airspace in accordance with flight instructions.NORAD, a joint US-Canadian military command, has intercepted more than 60 aircraft violating flight restrictions around Palm Beach since January last year.The Kyiv Post, citing The Telegraph, reported that federal court filings showed the Secret Service was seeking permanent flight restrictions around Mar-a-Lago.The filings cited concerns over potential terrorist threats and aerial intrusions. Secret Service Deputy Director Matthew Quinn described the threat profile in the documents as "heightened, real, and dynamic".Earlier security incidents involving TrumpTrump has faced several alleged threats to his life in recent years. In 2024, an armed man was found hiding in bushes along the perimeter of the president's Florida golf club.In February this year, a 21-year-old man drove through a gate at Mar-a-Lago carrying a shotgun before he was shot and killed.On many occasions, Iran has also threatened to harm Trump.The latest deployment also comes as Trump continues his campaign appearances ahead of the midterm elections.He was at Mar-a-Lago on Saturday after holding a rally in Daytona Beach on Friday and was scheduled to travel to Kansas and Iowa for further rallies on Sunday, according to The Independent.You use AI every day. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A consumer commission in Chandigarh has held two lenders responsible for the harassment of a man who was pursued for a Rs 30,000 loan he says
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A consumer commission in Chandigarh has held two lenders responsible for the harassment of a man who was pursued for a Rs 30,000 loan he says he never took. The loan was later found to be unauthorised. The commission directed CapFloat Financial Services, which operates under the brand name Axio, and Karur Vysya Bank to confirm he owes nothing, correct his credit record, and pay him Rs 25,000 as compensation and Rs 10,000 as litigation costs.In its order dated October 27, 2026, the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission-I, Chandigarh, held that the conduct of the two companies amounted to “gross deficiency in service and unfair trade practice.” It dismissed the complaint against Amazon Pay India.How the dispute aroseAccording to the order, the complainant, Daljeet Singh, a resident of Manimajra, received a text message in February 2024 demanding repayment of Rs 12,316 against a loan account. He said he had never applied for or availed of any such loan.When he enquired, CapFloat officials told him a credit facility of Rs 30,000 had been provided through Amazon Pay Later. He alleged that, despite his repeated requests and assurances, the company kept demanding repayment through recovery calls and threatening messages. He filed a police complaint on February 10, 2024.He later received summons from a Ludhiana court in recovery proceedings initiated by CapFloat for Rs 22,569. A legal notice dated April 20, 2025, then demanded Rs 32,694 as dues outstanding as of March 31, 2025.On April 27, 2025, he wrote to the company seeking documents on the loan application, sanction, disbursement and beneficiary account. In an email dated May 7, 2025, CapFloat said he had registered for Amazon Pay Later on January 14, 2024, and that 20 percent of the facility was funded by it and 80 percent by Karur Vysya Bank. It described the facility as a virtual line of credit, with no amount disbursed into any bank account.Singh alleged that the unauthorised loan and its adverse reporting in his CIBIL report hurt his creditworthiness and led another bank to refuse him a loan. The order does not record a finding on that last claim.What the companies saidCapFloat told the commission that its investigation identified the matter as an account takeover case involving an unauthorised transaction on Amazon’s platform. After confirmation from Amazon, it said, it waived the entire facility on June 18, 2025, without admitting liability.It also said it informed the credit bureaus and the co-lender about clearing the historical overdue entries and closing the account, and that the changes were expected to show in his credit profile within 30 to 45 working days. The order does not verify whether the updates took place.CapFloat and Karur Vysya Bank further said Singh declined to provide copies of his Aadhaar and PAN for internal verification, citing legal advice, even though the registered mobile number was linked to him in the company’s records. The commission did not rely on this point in its findings.Amazon Pay India said it could not trace any such loan using the mobile number provided and had no Amazon Pay Later account registered against it. It said it was only a facilitator and that CapFloat was responsible for clarifying the discrepancy.Karur Vysya Bank said the facility was offered under a co-lending arrangement with CapFloat, with the bank bearing 80 percent of the lending share and CapFloat 20 percent, and that CapFloat managed the accounting. It relied on CapFloat’s submission that the transaction had been found unauthorised and the loan waived.What the commission foundThe bench of president Pawanjit Singh and member Suresh Kumar Sardana noted that CapFloat, with Karur Vysya Bank relying on its submission, accepted that the transaction was an account takeover and that the complainant was not liable for the loan.The commission observed that these corrective steps came only after Singh had faced recovery demands and legal proceedings, and was at risk of damage to his creditworthiness. It noted that he had also approached the police and had to pursue the matter repeatedly to establish that he had not authorised the loan.“It is also observed that through things have been corrected & set in order by the OPs No.1 & 2 [sic; the order appears to mean OP Nos. 1 and 3], but these steps were taken only after the complainant had faced recovery demands, legal proceedings and the risk of damage to his creditworthiness,” the commission said.It added that the subsequent waiver “does not absolve” the opposite parties of responsibility for the “inconvenience, harassment and adverse consequences” suffered by the complainant due to the unauthorised transaction and its reporting to credit bureaus.Final orderCapFloat and Karur Vysya Bank, jointly and severally, must:Issue a certificate confirming zero outstanding liability on the disputed loan account.Rectify incorrect and adverse entries relating to the account with the credit bureaus and co-lenders.Pay Rs 25,000 as compensation for mental agony and harassment.Pay Rs 10,000 as litigation costs.They must comply within 45 days of receiving a certified copy of the order. If the compensation is not paid within that period, the Rs 25,000 will carry simple interest at 9 percent per annum from the date of the order until it is paid.The complaint against Amazon Pay India was dismissed.

articles.title: In 2002, Oprah Winfrey promised Nelson Mandela she would build a school for girls in South Africa; it opened in 2007, has graduated 528 students and will transfer to the government in 2027
articles.summary: For nearly two decades, the Oprah Winfrey Leadership Academy for Girls has provided education and boarding facilities to young women from disadvantaged
articles.body: For nearly two decades, the Oprah Winfrey Leadership Academy for Girls has provided education and boarding facilities to young women from disadvantaged backgrounds in South Africa. The school began with a conversation between Winfrey and Nelson Mandela in 2002, when the American television personality spoke about her intention to establish an institution for girls in the country. Five years later, the academy opened its doors near Johannesburg. Since then, it has produced hundreds of graduates, some of whom have gone on to careers in engineering, law, medicine and business. Now, Winfrey's original plan for the campus is approaching a new phase, with the property due to be handed over to local education authorities in 2027.How Nelson Mandela helped Oprah Winfrey turn her school vision into realityThe idea for the Oprah Winfrey Leadership Academy for Girls (OWLAG) took shape during a meeting between Winfrey and former South African President Nelson Mandela in 2002. The two were discussing poverty and the role education could play in addressing the inequalities that continued to affect communities across the country. Winfrey, who had grown up in poverty in the American South, spoke about wanting to establish a school for girls in South Africa.Mandela encouraged her to move ahead with the proposal, helping turn what had been a personal ambition into a project that could be realised within a few years. As reported by the BBC, the academy eventually opened in 2007 in Henley-on-Klip, a village south of Johannesburg in Gauteng province. Its purpose was to give academically capable girls from underprivileged households access to education and opportunities that might otherwise have remained beyond their reach.“I wanted to create an environment that I would want to be a part of.”The academy was intended to provide more than classroom teaching, with residential facilities and support designed around the needs of its pupils.Inside Oprah Winfrey's South African academy with its theatres, yoga studio and beauty salonThe academy was developed on a 52-acre site, with construction reportedly costing around $40 million. Its facilities included 21 classrooms, six laboratories, a library holding approximately 10,000 books and modern boarding accommodation. The campus also had a 600-seat theatre, landscaped outdoor areas and spaces for activities beyond the regular school curriculum.The scale of the development attracted attention when the institution opened. Reports about its facilities, which included two theatres, a yoga studio and a beauty salon, prompted questions about the amount spent on a single school. Some commentators argued that the same resources might have supported a larger number of children through educational programmes elsewhere in South Africa.The criticism formed part of the public discussion surrounding Oprah Winfrey Leadership Academy for Girls (OWLAG), although the academy continued operating and admitting students. Its residential model allowed girls from different parts of the country to study at the institution rather than having to travel daily to attend classes.More than 500 girls have graduated from the academyThe school's first graduating group completed its studies in 2012. Since then, the academy has built an alumni community whose members have pursued further education and careers in several fields. Oprah Winfrey Leadership Academy Foundation reported, 528 girls had graduated by the time of its 2020 impact report.The institution has reported that around 90% of its students go on to college or university. Alumni have attended universities in South Africa, the United States and Europe, including Spelman College, Oxford and Stanford.The school has also developed an alumni network. Established in 2020 and run by former students, the group had approximately 300 members at the time of the foundation's report. Its activities included mentoring, online discussions with speakers and work with non-profit organisations involved in South Africa's Covid-19 response.Oprah Winfrey's South African school faced allegations within its first yearOWLAG's history has not been without difficulties. Within months of its opening in 2007, allegations of abuse were made against a former member of staff by some students. The incident added to scrutiny of an institution that had already attracted debate over its construction costs and facilities. In the years that followed, the academy continued its educational programme, with its stated focus remaining on girls from disadvantaged communities.According to the BBC, there are currently 281 students enrolled at the school, according to the July 2026 announcement. Their education will be affected by the planned transition, although Winfrey's foundation has said that those who have not completed their studies by the time the campus closes will be offered full scholarships at other institutions.The campus will be handed over after the 2027 academic yearWinfrey announced on 30 July 2026 that the academy would stop operating at the end of the 2027 academic year. Under the original arrangement, the campus is due to be transferred to local education authorities at that point. The property will therefore return to the public education system rather than remain under the foundation's management.The announcement also addressed speculation circulating online about the reasons for the decision. A public relations consultant working with the Oprah Winfrey Leadership Academy Foundation rejected suggestions that the closure was linked to mismanagement. The foundation has presented the change as part of a transition from operating a single residential school to supporting talented girls through a wider scholarship programme.The Gauteng provincial education department has said it intends to maintain the institution's legacy once the property is handed over. However, the authorities have not yet announced precisely how the campus will be used after the transfer.Winfrey plans to continue supporting girls through scholarshipsThe end of the academy's residential school programme does not mean that Winfrey is withdrawing from education initiatives in South Africa. Her foundation intends to fund scholarships for academically gifted girls from communities across the country, enabling them to attend leading schools.The proposed approach would move the programme beyond one campus and allow support to reach students studying at different institutions. Girls who are currently enrolled at OWLAG but have yet to graduate will receive scholarship assistance to continue their education elsewhere.In her statement announcing the decision, Winfrey explained that the original ambition had extended beyond constructing a school building. She described the scholarship programme as the next stage of the work she began more than 20 years ago, with an emphasis on reaching young women in different parts of South Africa.You use AI every day. articles.title: Delhi's massive vehicle ban faces its biggest test at the borders: Can enforcement keep up?
articles.summary: Delhi’s decision to stop older vehicles not meeting BS6 norms from entering the capital brings the focus back to a challenge that is more than announcing
articles.body: Delhi’s decision to stop older vehicles not meeting BS6 norms from entering the capital brings the focus back to a challenge that is more than announcing restrictions, that of implementing them. With potentially more than 10 lakh vehicles from neighboring NCR cities affected, the success of the move will depend less on the rule itself, and more on how effectively authorities are able to identify, intercept and turn away vehicles at Delhi's numerous entry points.The exercise is on scale. Vehicles from Gurgaon, Faridabad, Noida, Greater Noida and Ghaziabad enter Delhi through a number of busy roads, many of which witness heavy traffic during morning and evening peak hours. It’s neither practical nor sustainable to check each vehicle manually. Even if teams from the traffic police and the transport department are deployed at major entry points, the volume of traffic could quickly overwhelm available manpower.The tech testTechnology will be important in enforcement, therefore. Cameras using automatic number plate recognition, linked to vehicle registration databases, can help to identify vehicles that do not meet prescribed emission standards. But the system will only work if the cameras cover key entry points, registration records are up to date and enforcement teams can act on the alerts as they happen.Practical complications also exist. Damaged, obscured or hard to read number plates can affect camera-based identification. Records of vehicles registered outside of Delhi may be incomplete or outdated. Authorities need to have a reliable way of checking these vehicles without increasing the level of congestion at the checkpoints.The gaps along the borderAnother challenge is the sheer number of ways in you can watch the major highways and arterial roads, but smaller roads and connecting stretches may be opportunities to get around the checkpoints. If the enforcement is focused on some high-profile spots, motorists could just find alternative routes into the city. It would also put traffic into residential areas and smaller roads, creating new congestion problems.Delhi and neighboring NCR authorities will have to coordinate equally. Data on vehicle registrations, emission certificates and enforcement should be accessible across the states. Without smooth coordination, vehicles turned away at one checkpoint might try to enter via another route. The exercise would be more effective if there is a common enforcement mechanism across the NCR.Commuters need to knowThe restrictions also have the potential to confuse daily commuters, especially those who travel to Delhi for work, education and business. Authorities will need to clearly communicate which vehicles are allowed, what documents drivers need to carry and how exemptions, if any, will be handled. It is equally important to ensure that enforcement is not arbitrary and that motorists do not face unnecessary delays or disputes at the checkpoints.Beyond the first crackdownThe larger question is whether enforcement can be maintained for the three-month restriction period, from Nov. 1 to Jan. 31. There will be a lot of activity at the initial deployment and checks but the real test will be to see if the monitoring continues at the same intensity after the first few weeks.Authorities should also regularly publish data on the number of vehicles checked, turned away and penalized and details of enforcement at different entry points. Such disclosures would help to ascertain whether the restrictions are being uniformly applied, or whether there are any gaps.In the end, Delhi’s vehicle ban is only as good as its enforcement network. A rule that appears strict on paper will be of little use if thousands of vehicles continue to pass through the borders. The administration will need more than checkpoints and occasional drives, already stressed by winter pollution. articles.title: Be a sport, give your eyes and back a rest: Prolonged gaming, binge-watching raise blood clot risks
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: From gaming marathons to back-to-back OTT episodes, hours spent glued to a screen may be doing more than straining the eyes and back.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: From gaming marathons to back-to-back OTT episodes, hours spent glued to a screen may be doing more than straining the eyes and back. Vascular experts warn that prolonged, uninterrupted sitting can slow blood flow in the legs and increase the risk of potentially dangerous blood clots, including deep vein thrombosis (DVT), even among younger people.At a conference being held in the city from Oct 8 to 10, experts said the concern was not gaming or OTT viewing itself, but the prolonged immobility that can accompany them.Dr Tapish Sahu, organising secretary of VSI-ASVS 2026 and head of vascular and endovascular surgery at Max Hospital, said doctors were seeing young patients with prolonged sitting and excessive screen exposure. "Sitting continuously for four to six hours while gaming or binge-watching leaves the calf muscles largely inactive. Movement breaks must become part of digital life," he said.A 2024 meta-analysis in Scientific Reports, analysing 31 studies, found that people with the highest sedentary behaviour had a 24% higher risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE) than those with the lowest levels. Risk rose by about 2% for every additional hour of daily sedentary behaviour.Dr Tarun Grover, senior director of peripheral vascular and endovascular sciences at Medanta, said immobility had traditionally been discussed in the context of long-distance travel, hospitalisation or being bedridden. "Today, we also need to ask young patients how many hours they spend continuously sitting in front of a gaming console, computer or OTT screen," he added.Experts cautioned that screen use does not automatically cause DVT, but prolonged sitting may add to the risk when combined with obesity, dehydration, smoking, hormonal factors, inherited clotting disorders or a previous history of thrombosis.A study published this year involving 11 adolescents with thrombosis found that they used digital devices for an average of six hours daily, with uninterrupted immobility averaging 2.7 hours. Eight had lower-limb DVT, two pulmonary embolism and one subclavian-vein thrombosis. Many also had inherited thrombophilia, suggesting that prolonged screen-related immobility may be an additional risk factor rather than the sole cause.Walking activates the calf muscles, which help pump blood towards the heart.Dr Bhupesh Garg, senior vascular and endovascular surgeon at the Vascular Society of India, said that "smoking adversely affects vascular health and increases thrombosis risk, while prolonged sitting slows blood flow from the legs due to calf muscle inactivity".The experts also stressed that regular exercise may not fully offset the risks of prolonged sitting. For young people, hours in classrooms followed by gaming, streaming or social media can add to their daily sedentary time.DVT occurs when a clot forms in a deep vein, usually in the leg. If it travels to the lungs, it can cause a potentially fatal pulmonary embolism. Swelling, pain or tenderness in one leg warrants medical evaluation, while sudden breathlessness, chest pain or coughing up blood requires urgent medical attention.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news.
