articles.title: A Georgia high-school student formed a volunteer team to turn backyards, schools and public spaces into wildlife habitat; two years later, Johns Creek became America’s 60th Certified Community Wildlife Habitat
articles.summary: A suburban Georgia community became a model for urban wildlife conservation after teenager Malcolm Barnard led a two-year campaign to turn backyards,
articles.body: A suburban Georgia community became a model for urban wildlife conservation after teenager Malcolm Barnard led a two-year campaign to turn backyards, school grounds and public spaces into wildlife habitats. According to the National Wildlife Federation (NWF), Johns Creek earned its Community Wildlife Habitat certification in 2012, becoming the organisation’s 60th certified community in the United States and only the second in Georgia at the time.Johns Creek, a growing city northeast of Atlanta, might not immediately seem like the setting for a major wildlife initiative. However, Barnard recognised the importance of protecting natural habitats in a rapidly developing suburban environment. According to National Wildlife magazine, he first discovered the NWF’s Community Wildlife Habitat programme while working on a school project. The programme encourages residents to make their properties more welcoming to wildlife by providing essential resources such as food, water, shelter and places where animals can raise their young. Inspired by the initiative, Barnard approached Johns Creek officials with the idea of pursuing certification for the entire city.The effort quickly grew beyond a student project. Barnard assembled a volunteer team and began working with residents, schools, businesses and community organisations. His approach included educating homeowners about wildlife-friendly gardening, encouraging individual properties to seek certification and organising workshops to build support for the initiative. Action for Nature, which later honoured Barnard with its 2013 International Young Eco-Hero award, said he also went door to door to explain why preserving habitat mattered in a rapidly developing community.The campaign also placed schools at the centre of the effort. Barnard secured funding that could be directed towards school habitat gardens, while participating schools received wildlife-habitat signage. By 2013, all 18 of Johns Creek’s public schools had become certified through the NWF’s Schoolyard Habitats programme, according to Action for Nature and other conservation records. The project required a significant amount of community participation. A contemporary local account reported that the certification effort involved hundreds of homes along with schools and community spaces. The aim was not simply to create isolated wildlife gardens, but to build a network of habitat across the city.That distinction mattered in a place experiencing rapid residential and commercial growth. Rather than treating wildlife conservation as something limited to parks or protected land, the Johns Creek initiative brought it into ordinary neighbourhoods, where gardens, schoolyards and shared spaces could collectively provide resources for birds, insects and other wildlife.Barnard’s work also began attracting attention beyond Johns Creek. In 2011, he was named one of four finalists for Atlanta’s Cox Conserves Heroes programme. Each finalist received $1,250 to support an environmental nonprofit or project, and Barnard directed his award toward his community habitat work, including grants for school gardens.The recognition continued after Johns Creek received its certification. In 2013, Barnard won first place in the 13-to-16 age category of Action for Nature’s International Young Eco-Hero Awards for his work organising the community around wildlife habitat. More than a decade later, the initiative has not disappeared. The NWF’s current community profile lists Johns Creek as an active certified community and records its original certification in April 2012, alongside subsequent recertification efforts. The city continues to work with local conservation partners to maintain its wildlife-habitat status.What began as a young person’s idea ultimately changed the way an entire suburb approached nature. In Johns Creek, conservation did not require setting the city aside from development. Instead, it meant finding ways for wildlife and everyday community life to coexist, one garden, school and shared space at a time.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: She struggled to find a job despite a postgraduate degree and faced rejection as a transgender woman; now 36-year-old Riyana Suree helps others find sponsors, education and a place to stay in Tamil Nadu
articles.summary: A postgraduate degree, a talent for dance and the determination to build a career did not make things easier for Riyana Suree.
articles.body: A postgraduate degree, a talent for dance and the determination to build a career did not make things easier for Riyana Suree. When the transgender woman approached private companies looking for a job, her qualifications were not enough to protect her from rejection. Even people who initially showed interest in learning dance from her reportedly changed their minds after discovering that she was transgender.Today, at 36, Riyana is working to ensure that other transgender people do not have to face the same barriers alone. Through the Thiru Aval Trust, she helps transgender students find educational sponsors, offers accommodation to those who have nowhere to stay and supports people looking for employment and livelihood opportunities.Her journey from struggling to find acceptance and professional opportunities to creating them for others is a story of turning personal setbacks into a larger purpose.A postgraduate degree, but no job opportunitiesBorn in Dindigul in 1990 and raised in Tiruchy, Riyana began recognising herself as a girl when she was 12. According to The New Indian Express, her journey as a transgender woman formally began in 2006. Her father, D Soosai Sagayam, worked in the cooperative sector, while her mother, Insiya Mary, is a homemaker.Acceptance within the family took time. Initially, she was not allowed to dress as a woman during family functions. Her sister-in-law, Gayathri Lenin, played an important role in helping the family understand and accept her identity.Academically, Riyana completed her bachelor's degree in Physics from St Joseph's College in Tiruchy and went on to pursue postgraduate studies at Jamal Mohamed College. She was also passionate about dance and had won several competitions.However, when she approached two or three private companies, including firms in the IT sector, for employment in 2013, she encountered repeated rejections.The experience affected her confidence to approach other organisations. She subsequently joined the Tamil Nadu State AIDS Control Society (TANSACS) as an outreach worker under a government programme, earning Rs 8,000 a month. She continued in the role for more than eight years, supplementing her income through dance performances and teaching.But even her interest in dance came with its own challenges.“Many people initially showed interest in joining my dance classes. But once they came to know that I was a transgender woman, several backed out,” she recalled, as reported by The New Indian Express.Riyana also attempted the TNPSC Group IV and railway recruitment examinations but could not clear them.A chance encounter opened the doors to modellingAn unexpected opportunity came in 2018. A photographer came across Riyana's photographs on Facebook and approached her for a photoshoot. The pictures attracted attention and gradually opened doors to modelling assignments and beauty pageants.She participated in several competitions, including Miss Trichy, Miss Koovagam, Miss Trans Queen India and Miss South India Trans. In 2023, she won the Miss Universe Trans India title at a competition held in New Delhi.The recognition gave her a platform beyond modelling. She now mentors contestants and conducts interview sessions in her capacity as the national director.However, while her own career was finding direction, Riyana had also begun thinking about how she could make opportunities more accessible to other transgender people.From opening her home to finding sponsors for studentsRiyana started the Thiru Aval Trust in 2019, which was officially registered in 2022. During the Covid-19 pandemic, she and her associates distributed food to transgender people and others in need. Over time, the initiative expanded to include education, employment, livelihood and medical assistance. Around 30 transgender people are associated with the trust.One of its important initiatives involves connecting transgender students with sponsors who can support their education.S Sayeesha, 27, from Tiruchy, is among those who received help. With Riyana's assistance in finding a sponsor, Sayeesha completed her MSc, BEd and teacher training. However, despite attending several interviews, she has not yet been able to secure a job in a private school and is preparing for government recruitment examinations, including TNPSC.“Although my family has accepted me, coming from an orthodox Muslim background, society has not. I have completed my studies and teacher training, but finding a job remains difficult,” Sayeesha said.Riyana's support has also extended beyond financial assistance. When Joshka Jasmine, 30, from Thanjavur, came to study at Government Law College in Tiruchy but had no place to stay, Riyana offered her a home. She also helped her find sponsors for her education.Joshka, who initially aspired to become a model, eventually chose law because she wanted to work for the transgender community and improve access to justice. She has been practising for two years and affectionately calls Riyana her 'mummy'.In another significant development, Joshka and Sowmiya Shashu, 37, were recently honoured at the 2026 convocation after graduating in 2024. They were the first transgender graduates to receive the honour since the college was established in 1980, according to The New Indian Express.Joshka also highlighted the community's long-standing demand for equal opportunities in education and employment.“We have been demanding horizontal reservation for the past 15 years and urge the state government to implement it,” she said.Creating opportunities where she once struggled to find themThe trust has also experimented with livelihood initiatives. Between 2021 and 2023, it ran a restaurant that employed five transgender people. It continues to distribute surplus food from functions and provides medical assistance, including support for transgender people living with HIV.Riyana now hopes to bring more organisations into these efforts and create opportunities in creative industries. In association with Iravi Trust, she is planning an LGBTQ-themed fashion runway in Tiruchy to showcase transgender talent.For her, the motivation comes from remembering the opportunities she could not access when she was starting out.“When I did not get an opportunity, I wanted to create one for someone else. That is the thought behind our efforts through the Thiru Aval Trust to support education, employment and livelihood,” she said.And while modelling titles and pageant recognition have marked important milestones in her own journey, Riyana says the real reward lies elsewhere.“The greatest satisfaction comes from seeing someone facing challenges like mine complete their education, get a job and live with self-respect,” she said.You use AI every day. articles.title: Oprah Winfrey helped launch a $60 million disaster-relief fund for Maui wildfire survivors; in June 2026, a separate donation delivered a new CT scanner to Maui Memorial Medical Center for local patients
articles.summary: Media mogul Oprah Winfrey has continued supporting residents of Hawaii’s Maui island, where devastating wildfires destroyed homes and displaced thousands
articles.body: Media mogul Oprah Winfrey has continued supporting residents of Hawaii’s Maui island, where devastating wildfires destroyed homes and displaced thousands of people in 2023. After joining actor Dwayne Johnson to launch the People’s Fund of Maui, which ultimately distributed $60 million to wildfire survivors, Winfrey made a separate contribution to healthcare in June 2026, helping Maui Memorial Medical Center acquire a new computed tomography (CT) scanner.According to Maui Health, the hospital system’s official announcement on June 12, 2026, Winfrey’s donation to the Maui Health Foundation made the advanced imaging equipment possible. The scanner was formally blessed during a ceremony on June 8, attended by Winfrey, members of the hospital’s imaging team and local spiritual leader Kahu Kimokeo Kapahulehua. The equipment is expected to strengthen access to diagnostic services for patients across Maui County.New CT scanner aims to improve diagnosis and treatmentThe new scanner at Maui Memorial Medical Center is designed to provide faster and more detailed medical images, helping physicians identify illnesses and make treatment decisions with greater precision. CT scans use X-rays and computer processing to produce detailed images of structures inside the body, helping doctors investigate injuries and diagnose a range of medical conditions. Maui Health said the new technology would help physicians diagnose and treat patients earlier and more accurately, while strengthening access to high-quality healthcare across the island county. The hospital’s imaging department will operate the equipment as part of its diagnostic services.The June 8 ceremony included a traditional blessing led by Kapahulehua. He blessed the scanner and the hands of the caregivers who would operate it, recognising the responsibilities of the imaging team in treating patients. Winfrey also joined the hospital staff during the event, marking the installation of equipment made possible by her contribution.The hospital expressed gratitude to Winfrey and her team for supporting the community’s healthcare needs. Neither the hospital’s announcement nor the local reports cited here disclosed the monetary value of her CT scanner donation.How Oprah Winfrey and Dwayne Johnson launched a $60 million relief fundWinfrey’s latest contribution follows a major relief initiative launched after the August 2023 Maui wildfires. The fires devastated Lahaina, a historic town on the island’s western coast, and caused widespread destruction, deaths and displacement. Residents faced the immediate loss of homes and belongings, alongside the longer-term challenges of finding housing and rebuilding their lives. On August 31, 2023, Winfrey and Johnson announced the People’s Fund of Maui, initially committing $10 million of their own money and inviting others to contribute. The initiative was designed to provide direct financial assistance to adults who had been displaced by the fires in Lahaina and Kula, allowing survivors to decide how best to use the money according to their individual circumstances.Under the programme, eligible adults were offered $1,200 per month during the distribution period. Rather than restricting assistance to specific purchases, the fund gave recipients flexibility to cover expenses such as housing, bills, transport and other immediate needs.The Entertainment Industry Foundation, which administered the fund, later reported that $60 million had been distributed to more than 8,100 residents. The final amount was substantially higher than the initial $10 million commitment announced at the fund’s launch.Direct payments offered survivors flexibilityThe fund’s approach was based on the idea that people affected by a disaster should have the freedom to decide which expenses were most urgent for them. Its administrators worked with local community leaders and elders while establishing the initiative, with the aim of reaching people who had lost their homes or whose homes had become uninhabitable.An Associated Press report published in April 2024 documented how the assistance helped survivors manage expenses while dealing with the aftermath of the fires. Some recipients used the money towards mortgage payments and essential household costs, while others faced vehicle repairs and the financial pressures associated with rebuilding their lives. The report also highlighted the scale of the continuing crisis. Thousands of people had been displaced, and survivors continued to confront housing shortages, prolonged stays in temporary accommodation and the emotional toll of losing homes and community connections. The relief payments offered a measure of financial flexibility, but they could not resolve the broader challenges of recovery.A separate contribution to Maui’s healthcare needsWinfrey’s June 2026 donation to the Maui Health Foundation represents a separate form of support, focused on medical infrastructure rather than direct cash payments to wildfire survivors. The new scanner is intended to benefit patients across Maui County, not exclusively those affected by the fires.The donation also comes amid wider efforts to strengthen the island’s healthcare facilities. In September 2026, Maui Health Foundation announced that three donors had secured $4.1 million for a new MRI system at Maui Memorial Medical Center. The Oprah Winfrey Charitable Foundation contributed $500,000 towards that project, alongside funding from the Stable Road Foundation and Maui residents Nan and Wayne Kocourek.You use AI every day. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Three Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leaders from Punjab, including rebel MLAs Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra and Chetan Singh Jouramajra, joined the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Monday, days after breaking ties with the Arvind Kejriwal-led party. The third leader is suspended AAP MLA and former IPS officer Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh, who also resigned from the Punjab Assembly on Monday.Pathanmajra and Jouramajra were seen raising slogans of 'BJP zindabad' at the BJP headquarters in Delhi, according to a video shared by news agency ANI.The development comes a day after Pathanmajra, who represents the Sanour constituency, and Jouramajra, the MLA from Samana in Punjab's Patiala district, resigned from the primary membership of the AAP. Both leaders had accused the Bhagwant Mann-led government of failing to address issues such as the drug menace, rising state debt and governance-related concerns.Their exits came shortly after the AAP released its first list of 40 candidates for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections. Neither Sanour nor Samana figured in the list.AAP had said it would approach the Punjab Assembly Speaker seeking cancellation of the legislative membership of both MLAs, alleging that they had engaged in anti-party activities. The party had suspended both leaders before they announced their resignations.Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh resigns as Punjab MLAThe political developments also saw suspended AAP MLA and former IPS officer Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh resign from the Punjab Assembly. Singh, who represents Amritsar North, submitted his resignation to assembly Speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan.In a Facebook post, Singh announced his decision, stating, "I have resigned from the membership of Punjab Vidhan Sabha."In his resignation letter to the Speaker, he wrote, "I hereby tender my resignation of my seat in the House with effect from 1.11.2026."Singh was suspended from the AAP for five years in June 2025 over alleged anti-party activities. His suspension followed his criticism of the Punjab Vigilance Bureau's action against Shiromani Akali Dal leader Bikram Singh Majithia.A former member of the Punjab Police special investigation team (SIT) that probed the 2015 Kotkapura and Behbal Kalan police-firing incidents, Singh had repeatedly questioned the Mann government's handling of the sacrilege cases.AAP targets BJP over induction of rebel leadersThe BJP's induction of the rebel AAP leaders has drawn criticism from the ruling party in Punjab. Punjab AAP president Aman Arora accused the BJP of attempting to induct leaders who had left or been expelled from other parties.AAP chief spokesperson Kuldeep Singh Dhaliwal had also described the BJP as a 'kabaad di dukaan' (scrap shop), accusing it of collecting rejected political faces.Before announcing his resignation, Pathanmajra had said that the two leaders would join a party that worked in the interest of Punjab.Jouramajra, a former Punjab minister, served in the Bhagwant Mann cabinet from January 2023 to September 2024 before being dropped during a cabinet reshuffle.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Shakira's Barefoot Foundation has supported over 224,000 disadvantaged children, with 8 in 10 graduates pursuing higher education; its funding is building schools, training teachers and supporting Indigenous communities
articles.summary: Shakira's Barefoot Foundation has supported more than 224,000 children and young people in Colombia, helping expand access to education through school
articles.body: Shakira's Barefoot Foundation has supported more than 224,000 children and young people in Colombia, helping expand access to education through school construction, teacher training and educational programmes. Founded by the Colombian singer in 1997, Fundación Pies Descalzos works with communities facing economic and social barriers to quality education. The organisation reports that 8 in 10 students graduating from its supported schools continue to higher education, compared with approximately four in 10 young people nationally. Its work also includes improving educational facilities in underserved areas, providing school supplies and supporting Indigenous communities.Shakira's foundation focuses on education as a path out of inequalityShakira established Fundación Pies Descalzos in 1997 to help children in Colombia access quality education. The organisation, also known as the Barefoot Foundation, focuses on children and young people in vulnerable communities, where financial difficulties and limited educational infrastructure can restrict opportunities.Rather than concentrating exclusively on school construction, the foundation combines infrastructure projects with teacher training, educational support and programmes intended to help students continue their studies.Its approach also involves working with public schools and local communities to improve learning environments. According to the foundation, its projects aim to ensure that children can develop the knowledge and skills needed to pursue further education and build better prospects for themselves and their families.Eight in 10 graduates continue to higher educationOne of the foundation's most notable reported outcomes is the proportion of students who continue their education after graduating from its supported schools.According to its official impact page, eight in 10 graduates from Pies Descalzos schools continue to higher education. The foundation contrasts this with the national picture, citing data from Colombia's National Administrative Department of Statistics (DANE) indicating that approximately four in 10 young people continue to this level of education.In a November 2025 publication, the foundation said between 70% and 80% of students graduating from schools it supports continue into tertiary education. This includes technical, technological and university-level programmes.Building schools in underserved communitiesImproving access to educational infrastructure is a central part of the foundation's work. Its projects include constructing new schools and upgrading existing facilities in areas where children face barriers to quality education.In 2024, the foundation reported supporting 28,157 students across 24 Colombian municipalities through educational and school-infrastructure projects. This was in addition to approximately 6,700 children and young people enrolled in schools supported by the organisation and bearing its name.One of its projects that year was a new school in the Villas de Aranjuez neighbourhood of Cartagena. The facility was designed to serve approximately 1,000 students annually, helping expand educational provision in the area.The foundation also worked with Colombia's Ministry of National Education to improve two schools in Riohacha and Uribia, in the department of La Guajira. These projects focused on strengthening educational access for communities that include Indigenous students and migrants.Supporting Indigenous Wayúu students and migrant familiesIn 2024, the organisation and Colombia's Ministry of National Education completed interventions at two schools in Riohacha and Uribia. The facilities served more than 1,500 students, most of whom belonged to the Wayúu Indigenous community or were migrants from Venezuela.The projects used an ethno-educational approach, recognising the importance of cultural context in education. This is particularly relevant for Indigenous communities, where education programmes must account for local identities and circumstances.Training teachers and providing learning materialsThe foundation also invests in teachers, recognising that educational facilities alone cannot guarantee effective learning.Its official impact figures report that more than 12,824 teachers have received training, with women accounting for 85% of those trained. The organisation says these programmes are intended to strengthen teaching practices and help educators introduce new skills into their classrooms.In 2024, the foundation reported that 690 teachers participated in its training programmes.The organisation also distributed 10,965 kits, uniforms and reading materials to students, teachers, school leaders and coordinators that year. Such supplies can help schools and families meet some of the practical requirements of education.These initiatives complement the foundation's infrastructure projects by supporting the people and resources involved in students' day-to-day learning.Foundation reports more than 282,000 beneficiariesAlthough the foundation's impact page reports that it has supported more than 224,000 children and young people, its English-language homepage now lists a higher cumulative figure.The homepage reports more than 282,160 children and young people benefited, over 13,387 teachers trained and more than 300 public schools supported in Colombia. It also lists 22 schools built or improved in Colombia, two in Haiti and one in Soweto.The foundation also reports working with 1,131 families and caregivers, 80% of whom are women, according to its impact page. This highlights another dimension of its work: involving families in supporting children's development and education.Shakira's foundation expands support beyond the classroomThe organisation's work has also extended into partnerships intended to help young people navigate education and prepare for their futures.In April 2026, Colombia's student-loan and educational-support agency ICETEX announced a three-year partnership with Fundación Pies Descalzos under its Comunidad ICETEX project.The collaboration aims to support young people as they prepare for higher education, continue their studies and move towards employment. Its planned areas of work include financial education, emotional wellbeing, career guidance, gender equality, entrepreneurship, leadership and employability.You use AI every day.
